apr annual percentage rate is a standardized way to express the true yearly cost of borrowing money unlike a simple interest rate apr folds in fees charged by the lender giving you a single number that reflects what you actually pay per year relative to the amount borrowed lenders in the us are required by the truth in lending act tila to disclose apr on consumer loans making it the most consistent basis for comparing offers from different banks or credit unions car buyers comparing dealer financing to a credit union loan homeowners evaluating refinance offers and credit card holders weighing balance transfer options all benefit from understanding apr this calculator estimates apr by combining the loan amount stated interest rate total fees and loan term into a single annualized figure

a borrower takes a 25000 auto loan at 65 interest for 60 months with a 400 origination fee the stated monthly payment is about 487 total interest over 60 months is roughly 4220 adding the 400 fee gives a total finance charge of 4620 the apr works out to approximately 69 about 04 percentage points higher than the stated rate a competing lender offers 68 with no fees that loans apr is 68 actually worse than the first offer despite the higher stated rate because the first offers apr of 69 is only marginally higher and the first lender may offer better service terms comparing aprs side by side makes this kind of nuanced analysis straightforward

the interest rate is the cost of borrowing the principal only expressed as a yearly percentage apr includes the interest rate plus most fees origination fees broker fees and certain closing costs spread over the loan term apr is always equal to or higher than the stated rate comparing aprs across lenders gives you a more applestoapples view of total borrowing cost than comparing interest rates alone

credit card apr represents the annual interest rate charged on balances you carry month to month most cards use daily periodic rate compounding so the actual effective rate is slightly higher than the stated apr if you pay your full balance every month apr is irrelevant since no interest accrues apr matters most when you carry a revolving balance even a few percentage points difference compounds significantly over months

sitdown restaurants 1820 for standard service 2225 for exceptional service 15 is generally considered acceptable for merely adequate service but falls below current expectations at most fullservice restaurants

tipping is not legally required but it is a deeply embedded social norm federal law allows tipped workers to be paid as little as 213 per hour with tips expected to make up the difference to minimum wage not tipping in a sitdown restaurant is viewed as a significant social slight

many restaurants require servers to share a portion of their tips with support staff such as bussers food runners bartenders and hosts your server may keep only 6070 of tips after the tipout tipping generously benefits the entire service team

expectations are lower for counter service and takeout than for table service a tip of 1015 or simply rounding up is common and appreciated skipping entirely is socially acceptable though any amount left helps
10 of any amount is simply moving the decimal one place left double it for 20 for 18 take 20 and subtract 10 of that result on a 75 bill 20 1500 minus 150 1350 for an 18 tip
